newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares at the whim of weary Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: German shares at the whim of weary Wall Street.

text.p: German traders kept a wary eye on Wall Street in late Monday trade as the DAX index remained down amid new selling pressure on the Dow Jones index.

The IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day electronic dealings, was down 40.40 points at 3,278.84 points and about equal with the bourse session close when the DAX ended down 60.15 points at 3,279.90 in reaction to last Friday's Dow Jones index drop.
An initial firmer opening on Wall Street gave way to losses and the DAX followed despite a firmer dollar.
"Our movements for now are going to depend on Wall Street and the dollar, that's where we are looking," said one trader.
Traders said they were eyeing support for the DAX at 3,200 points -- a level they said could be reached this week.

But Germany's Trinkaus Capital Management said in a report issued on Monday that the DAX's correction could open up opportunities for fresh buying, noting downside risk in U.S. market was "no longer all that great".
The Trinkaus report said the recent trading range of 3,200 to 3,400 points in the DAX "should continue to exist".
"On the whole, we see little danger of a heavy setback on the German equity market," it said. "It is quite possible that the lower limit will be reached in the next few days."

Among specific shares, drugs and chemicals group Merck rose five pfennigs at 67.25 marks in late trade after reporting first quarter sales were up 12.4 percent to 1.896 billion marks and strong growth in its pharmaceuticals unit.
Carmaker Volkswagen AG, which surged last week on its 1997 outlook, was down one mark at 1,052 marks, holding up relatively well despite the overall market downturn.

Industrial group Daimler-Benz AG was down 50 pfennigs at 135 marks. Daimler, which builds Mercedes cars, said it would take a 25 percent stake in Canada-based Ballard Power Systems, to develop alternative fuel engines.
